prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary (max 500 words)

Economy and public finances
- Balance the structural current budget by 2017/18; debt to fall as a share of GDP thereafter. New fiscal rules allow borrowing for productive investment while balancing day-to-day spending over the cycle.
- Raise the Personal Allowance to at least £12,500; consider aligning the employee National Insurance threshold afterwards.
- Fund deficit reduction partly via measures targeting tax avoidance/evasion, a continued banking levy, reforms to capital gains/dividend reliefs, a banded levy on residential properties over £2m, and tighter non‑dom rules; no rises in headline Income Tax, VAT, NI or Corporation Tax rates.
- Maintain 0.7% of GNI for international development.

Jobs, industry, banking and tech
- Expand an Industrial Strategy; aim to double economy‑wide innovation/R&D; grow advanced apprenticeships and create sectoral National Colleges.
- Strengthen the British Business Bank; promote competition, community and alternative finance; complete retail/investment bank separation.
- Complete high‑speed broadband rollout (99.9% coverage); support regional tech clusters; expand open data and digital public services.

Energy, climate and environment
- Legally binding target for net‑zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050; power‑sector decarbonisation range for 2030 (50–100g CO2/kWh) with indicative 60% renewables.
- End unabated coal power by 2025; expand CCS, storage, smart grids; support community energy; accept new nuclear subject to safety, waste and cost tests without subsidy.
- Tight fracking regulation; dedicate 50% of shale tax revenues to a Low‑carbon Transition Fund.
- Five “green laws” package: Nature Act, Resource Efficiency/Zero Waste (70% recycling target; landfill/incineration reforms), Green Transport (ULEV-only new cars on roads by 2040; rail electrification), Zero Carbon Britain, and Green Buildings (home EPC targets; council tax incentive for insulation).
- Expand accessible green space, marine protections, pollinator safeguards, and water metering in stressed areas.

Transport and housing
- HS2 as part of a wider high‑speed network; major rail electrification; East–West Rail; Transport for the North; support light rail; shift freight to rail; Low Emission Zones; cycling investment; bus reform and smart ticketing.
- Build up to 300,000 homes a year; at least 10 Garden Cities; use public land; commission building where markets under‑deliver; Housing Investment Bank.
- Strengthen planning (15‑year plans, brownfield priority, self‑build registers); more affordable housing; “Rent to Own” and “Help to Rent”; longer tenancies with predictable rents; stronger landlord standards.

Tax, welfare, work and pensions
- Universal Credit rollout with sanctions reform (“yellow card” first); 1% cap on most working‑age benefits until 2017/18; restrict some pensioner benefits for higher‑rate taxpayers.
- Expand free childcare towards 20 hours (ages 2–4; from 9 months for working parents); complete Tax‑Free Childcare.
- Enforce minimum wage; promote Living Wage in central government; enhance flexible and shared parental leave.
- Maintain the State Pension “triple lock”; complete single‑tier pension; continue auto‑enrolment; extend pension flexibilities.

Education and skills
- Protect education funding from early years to 19; increase Early Years Pupil Premium; qualified teachers in every class; independent curriculum/standards body; core PSHE including financial literacy and consent.
- Target ending child illiteracy/innumeracy by 2025; strengthen school leadership and fair admissions; extend free school meals to all primary (subject to resources).
- Double the number of employers taking apprentices; grow higher apprenticeships; improve FE and a credit transfer system in HE; review student finance.

Health and social care
- Increase NHS England funding by at least £8bn real terms by 2020; expand GP access; integrate health and social care budgets locally by 2018.
- Parity for mental health: waiting‑time standards (e.g., 6 weeks for talking therapies; 2 weeks for first‑episode psychosis); additional funding including for children’s services.
- Carers package: £250 annual bonus; explore paid care leave; identification and support duties for the NHS.
- Implement care‑cost cap; raise care workforce standards; promote Living Wage.

Rights, policing, justice, drugs
- Digital Bill of Rights; protect Human Rights Act; updated surveillance oversight.
- Replace Police and Crime Commissioners with Police Boards; Victims’ Bill of Rights; stronger action on domestic/sexual violence and FGM.
- Presumption against short prison sentences; expand community and problem‑solving courts; youth and women’s justice boards; legal aid and court fee reviews.
- Treat personal drug possession primarily as a health issue (Portugal‑style diversion); allow medicinal cannabis.

Borders, devolution, democracy, international
- Restore full entry/exit checks; faster asylum decisions; allow work after six months; separate students in migration stats.
- Constitutional convention; votes at 16; proportional voting (STV) for local and national elections; House of Lords reform; donation cap of £10,000.
- Implement further devolution to Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland; “Devolution on Demand” within England; fair funding floor for Wales.
- Remain engaged in EU; deepen Single Market; support trade deals with safeguards; cross‑border crime tools; uphold free movement with tighter benefit rules.
- SDSR with a Single Security Budget; adjust nuclear posture away from continuous patrols; strengthen cyber and veterans’ support.
- Maintain 0.7% aid; focus on conflict prevention, climate diplomacy, anti‑tax avoidance, human rights, and marine/forestry protection.
